description: Language-agnostic specification for the decodability evaluation. Defines, per language, what 'decodable' means, which orthographic unit categories and reason codes are legal, and (for sw) a reference inventory used by the validator's heuristic decodability cross-check. Items reference a student_id; students reference a language; this file is the contract both are validated against.

field_definitions.student.language: ISO code; selects which block of `languages` applies.
field_definitions.student.description: Human-readable summary of what the student has been taught.
field_definitions.student.known_graphemes: Object whose keys are unit categories. The legal keys are language-dependent (see languages[lang].unit_categories). A category present as a list (possibly empty []) means 'applies to this language; student knows these'. A category set to null means 'not applicable to this language'. Empty list != null.
field_definitions.student.sight_words: Whole words the student recognises on sight even if not decodable from known units. These RESCUE otherwise-undecodable words and must NOT be flagged.
field_definitions.item.language: Must match the referenced student's language.
field_definitions.item.text: Stimulus passage shown to the model under test.
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words: Ground-truth answer key: words in `text` that are neither decodable from the student's known units nor a known sight word. The key is specific to this (text x student) pairing.
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words[].frequency: Occurrences of the word in `text` (see conventions.frequency).
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words[].offending_units: Specific untaught unit(s) that make the word undecodable. Syllabic nasals are written with the combining mark (m followed by U+0329).
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words[].reason_categori: One or more codes from languages[lang].reason_categories.

conventions.frequency: Case-insensitive count of the word among whitespace-delimited tokens in `text`, after stripping surrounding punctuation. Word-internal apostrophes are preserved (so ng'ombe is one token).
conventions.tokenization: Split on whitespace; strip the characters . , ! ? ; : " ( ) from each end; do not strip apostrophes; lowercase.
conventions.accessibility: A word is ACCESSIBLE (not flagged) iff it is a known sight word OR every unit in a valid segmentation is in the student's known set. Otherwise it is UNDECODABLE.
conventions.syllabification_note: Words with contested syllable boundaries should be excluded from answer keys, or annotated, so labels stay unambiguous.

sw.decodability_rule: Kiswahili orthography is transparent and predominantly open-CV. A word is accessible to the student iff it is a known sight word, OR it can be segmented into syllables (standalone vowel V; onset+vowel where the onset is a single consonant, digraph, nasal/prenasalized cluster, or consonant+glide; or a syllabic nasal) such that every unit used is in the student's known_graphemes. There are very few irregular words, so sight_words is a small safety valve rather than a primary mechanism.

reference_inventory.comment: Full inventory of sw orthographic units, independent of any student. Used by the validator's heuristic segmenter to cross-check answer keys. Syllabic nasals (m, n before a consonant) are handled by rule, not listed here.

en.decodability_rule: English orthography is opaque, so decodability is defined over grapheme-phoneme correspondences (GPCs) and syllable types rather than syllable set-membership. A word is accessible iff it is a known sight/heart word, OR it can be segmented into known GPCs and known syllable types. Because many high-frequency words are irregular, sight_words carries far more weight than in sw.

reference_inventory.comment: Placeholder. No en students or items exist yet; this block documents that the sw-specific categories (syllabic_nasals, nasal_prenasalized_onsets, consonant_glide_onsets) are simply absent here, and en introduces categories sw lacks. A separate en decoder would be needed for the heuristic cross-check.
